deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 52–54): a topological space X is given together with a family of closed subspaces (X_i)_{i∈I} indexed by a poset I, encoded simplicially. X_{Δ0} = ⊔ X_i, X_{Δ1} ⊂ X_{Δ0}×X_{Δ0} is the 'incidence' relation, and X = lim_I X_i. Conditions (21 a–d) are stated on an earlier page. Judging from their use here, (a) is local finiteness, and (d) is a pointwise codirectedness condition: for every x, the set I_x = {i : x ∈ X_i} is filtered decreasing.

The question: should (21 d) be strengthened to the lattice-type condition (24)? That condition asks that for all i, j the meet i∧j exists and X_{i∧j} = X_i ∩ X_j.

Grothendieck answers no, with an example. Take a circle stratified by two closed arcs A and B meeting in two points {a} and {b}. The poset is {a}, {b} < A, B, and A∧B does not exist. Now take the cone with vertex o. This gives a local stratification at o with five strata: o, the two cone-rays oa and ob, and the two cone-sectors over A and B. Two connected closed strata (the cones on A and B) meet in a set that, away from o, is disconnected (the two rays), and they have no meet in I. Such a cone on a link is a perfectly reasonable local model, so (24) should not be imposed: 'la suite le montrera bien'.

He then shows that the pointwise condition suffices for the basic construction. By (21a), I_x is finite. By (21d), I_x is filtered decreasing. Hence I_x has a least element i(x), the smallest i with x ∈ X_i (25).

On the next page this yields the open strata X_i^* = X_i \ ∪_{j<i} X_j. These partition X, with x ∈ X_{i(x)}^*. In modern terms, x ↦ i(x) is a continuous map X → I for the Alexandrov topology in which down-sets are closed. That is, (X_i) is the system of closures-of-strata of a poset-stratified space, and only a 'frontier condition' type of compatibility is required, not a lattice structure on I.
errors: Minor imprecision: the intersection cone(A) ∩ cone(B) = cone(a) ∪ cone(b) is connected (the two rays meet at o). It is disconnected only after removing o, i.e. on the link. The real point of the example is that A∧B does not exist in the poset, so (24) fails.
The transcription duplicates the 'filtrant ... décroissant par (21 d)' line. The argument itself is fine: a finite codirected set has a least element.

ideas.what: Stratified space given as a locally finite system of closed subspaces indexed by a poset, glued as a colimit/simplicial object (X_{Δr})
ideas.modern_name: poset-stratified space (continuous map to a poset with Alexandrov topology); closed-cover nerve presentation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A, 2010s); earlier Thom–Mather, Goresky–MacPherson
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions a programme of 'dévissage' of stratified structures but not this formalism

ideas.what: Rejecting the lattice/meet condition (24) in favour of pointwise codirectedness of I_x, justified by a cone-on-link example where two strata meet in two points
ideas.modern_name: frontier condition without lattice hypothesis; conical (cone-on-link) local models
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather; regular CW complexes)

ideas.what: i(x) = least index with x ∈ X_i, giving the partition into open strata X_i^*
ideas.modern_name: stratification map X → P; strata as fibres

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine foundational choice: no lattice condition is imposed on the stratifying poset, motivated by cones on links. It matches what later poset-stratified frameworks (e.g. Lurie) adopted. It is historically mildly interesting as an early formulation, but nothing here is new to specialists.
